en.runTitle: Chicago renter with dust and pollen allergies: air purifiers under $300 for a 300 sq ft bedroom

fields.label: Open-door layout
fields.placeholder: e.g. bedroom door usually open to the hallway

fields.label: Noise tolerance
fields.placeholder: e.g. must be near-silent on the setting I sleep on

en.template: Compare US air purifiers for my {zip}, {room}, {layout}, {noise} and {budget}. Check exact model revisions, per-speed noise and CADR evidence, genuine filter costs, delivered totals and return terms for {month}. Keep ozone/ionizer limits and unknowns clear. Plan only; do not buy, create accounts or contact sellers.

phases.title: Check public prices, specifications, filters, and safety and sizing guidance
phases.note: EPA and California guidance on ozone and ionizers, plus each maker’s own pages
phases.judgment: A researcher was asked for two models and reported that neither could be recommended as a current purchase: Winix’s 5510 product page is gone, and Honeywell’s store lists its model as discontinued. They refused to treat old indexed prices as live offers, and a follow-up found a replacement that could be verified, the Winix 5520 at $259.99, in stock.

phases.title: Write the practical comparison page and a dated source list
phases.note: Six models, sizing, safety, two recommendations
phases.judgment: It flagged where the budget is tight: the stronger Core 600S-P is $299.99, so it only fits under $300 before tax. It also flagged the airflow limits at quiet settings and that March 2027 prices are uncertain.

phases.title: Check the calculations, links and final files
phases.judgment: The independent reviewer found one sentence that was too sweeping, that all six models clear the sizing target, when the figures for two brands with their ionizers switched off were not established. They proposed rewording it to say only what the published figures show.
